# Data Sync lost its GitHub corpus stage in the split and stayed green

Refs #17834

## Context

`#17834` has been breaching for **five days** with no assignee and no root-cause ticket. Its alarm body says *"runs fail on schedule and nothing else surfaces it"* — that line is template prose, and it is **wrong**. The runs do not fail. The watchdog's own numbers say so: **Streak: 0 consecutive failures**, last success [2026-08-31T04:59:32Z](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33358946463). Only the staleness axis fires, and only into a bot-maintained alarm nobody owns.

@neo-opus-vega cleared this for repair on 2026-08-29 (`#17834` comment), settling the D#17846 OQ5 worry: every surviving content-sync design still needs the single-repo corpus this stage regenerates — the options relocate its output, none discard the stage. Repairing now is not work anyone throws away. That clearance has sat unclaimed for two days.

## The Problem

`buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs` ran three emission stages. It now runs two.

`c623b2f63c` — *"feat(engine): remove received Brain implementation (#17791) (#17806)"*, 2026-08-26 22:28 UTC — removed exactly one entry from `emissionCommands`:

```js
args      : ['./ai/scripts/maintenance/syncGithubWorkflow.mjs', '--emit-only'],
command   : process.execPath,
label     : 'GitHub Workflow corpus',
tokenScope: 'reader'
```

That stage is the **only** producer of `resources/content/{issues,pulls,discussions}`. Its script moved to the Brain in the split, so the entry could not survive — but nothing replaced it, and nothing failed when it went.

**What the pipeline does now, per run [33358946463](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33358946463):**

```
[DataSync] emit attempt=1 stage=install dependencies credential=none
[DataSync] emit attempt=1 stage=content indexes and SEO credential=reader
[DataSync] publish attempt=1/2 result=no-generated-changes
```

Two stages, both succeed, `no-generated-changes`, exit 0.

**Why this is worse than a stopped pipeline.** The surviving `content indexes and SEO` stage still *reads* `resources/content/issues`, `.../pulls`, `.../discussions` and writes the portal's chunked indexes, id maps and crawler manifests from them. It has been deriving portal data from a five-day-old corpus and committing it, so the pipeline keeps producing `chore(data): Hourly data sync pipeline update` commits — most recently `7ecd6b8b6e` on 2026-08-30 12:44 UTC. **"The pipeline stopped committing" is false.** It commits derived artifacts on schedule and has not touched the three source facets since:

| facet | last commit on `origin/dev` | commit |
|---|---|---|
| `issues` | 2026-08-26T19:33:00Z | `e7874db2d2` |
| `pulls` | 2026-08-26T16:39:44Z | `514c6709bb` |
| `discussions` | 2026-08-26T15:12:45Z | `294a7a31d9` |

A green pipeline, fresh derived commits, and a frozen source. Anyone reading run status or commit recency concludes it is healthy.

**Who is hurt.** `resources/content/**` is the substrate `ticket-create` §1a greps for duplicate detection. @neo-opus-vega broadcast on 2026-08-28 that the grep is blind to everything since 08-26 and that the live GitHub sweep is currently the only working duplicate gate. Every seat has been running a five-day-stale local dup gate since, and the KB ingestion behind it is stale by the same amount.

**The family.** This is the third load-bearing mechanism removed as `#17791` collateral and discovered only by its silence:

| mechanism | removed by | discovered |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-pr-body-lint.yml` | `91ae3604b4` | #17916 — after an unenforced body reached `dev` |
| seat lifecycle hooks | `c623b2f63c` | `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#250` — Stop gate exiting 1, non-blocking, silent |
| GitHub corpus emission | `c623b2f63c` | here — five days of a green pipeline over a frozen corpus |

Same commit as the hooks, same shape: the removal set was censused for what *moved*, never for Engine-side consumers left pointing at the hole. Each failed **open**.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:64–81` — `emissionCommands`, now two entries; the removed third is recoverable from `c623b2f63c^`.
- `.github/workflows/data-sync-pipeline.yml:115–119` — invokes the pipeline; `:120–183` pushes derived output to `neomjs/pages`. Neither knows a stage is missing.
- `buildScripts/dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` — measures run status **and** committed-corpus age on separate axes. The two-axis design is what caught this at all; the run-status axis alone would still read green today. That design is correct and is not what needs changing.
- The script now lives at `neo-agent-brain` `ai/scripts/maintenance/syncGithubWorkflow.mjs`, exposed as `ai:sync-github-workflow`.
- `neomjs/neo` `package.json` declares **no** dependency on `neo-agent-brain`, and ADR 0040 §2.3 fixes the direction: the Agent OS consumes the **published Engine**, never the reverse.

So the stage cannot simply be restored in place. Its script is on the other side of a boundary that only permits traffic the other way.

## The Fix

Restore GitHub corpus emission under an owner that may legally run it, and make its absence loud.

1. **Emission moves to the side that owns the script.** The Brain runs `syncGithubWorkflow.mjs --emit-only` on its own schedule and publishes the three facets into this repository. Brain→Engine is the permitted direction under §2.3; an Engine-side `import` of Brain substrate is not, and re-adding the deleted entry verbatim would re-create the dependency the split removed.
2. **The Engine pipeline keeps derivation only** — `content indexes and SEO` stays here and continues to read the corpus. Its input becomes a published artifact rather than a same-run sibling stage.
3. **Derivation refuses a stale input rather than deriving from it.** Today it silently rebuilds the portal from whatever age the corpus happens to be. It should fail, or at minimum emit a loud non-green signal, when the facets it reads are older than the **effective corpus-age band** — `resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()`, default **48h**, overridable via `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS`. This is the guard that would have surfaced the break on day two instead of day five.

   The band is 48h rather than the hourly cadence because **a facet only commits when GitHub content actually changed**: a cadence-tight threshold breaches on every quiet night and weekend, and a guard that cries wolf daily is muted within a day. A tighter bound needs a producer that emits a heartbeat even when nothing changed — so the corpus can be proven *current* rather than merely *recently changed* — and that producer lives in the Agent OS repository, out of scope here.
4. **A stage-set assertion.** The pipeline asserts the emission stages it expects to run, so a stage vanishing from `emissionCommands` is a red run, not a shorter one. `no-generated-changes` must not be reachable by *having no generator*.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `resources/content/{issues,pulls,discussions}` | ADR 0040 §2.3 (Agent OS consumes the published Engine) | produced by the Brain-side scheduled emission, published into this repository | none — an absent producer is a red pipeline, never a quiet `no-generated-changes` | pipeline JSDoc + `#17834` alarm body | facet commit ages move on the cadence, asserted against a mutant that removes the producer |
| `emissionCommands` stage set | this ticket | asserted by label; a missing expected stage fails the run | none | `dataSyncPipeline.mjs` JSDoc | negative control: delete a stage entry, run must go red |
| `content indexes and SEO` input | this ticket | refuses to derive from a corpus older than the effective corpus-age band — `resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()`, default **48h**, overridable via `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` | none — deriving from stale input is the defect | stage JSDoc | negative control: age the corpus past the band, stage must not report success |
| corpus-age **policy** | this ticket | `resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()` is the single resolution site; every consumer resolves through it **per call**, never through the constant. Sharing a default is not sharing policy: while the guard imported `DEFAULT_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` and the alarm resolved the override, `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS=72` had a 60h corpus rejected by one and reported `{breached: false}` by the other | none | `dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` JSDoc | negative control: set the override, assert guard and alarm agree about the same corpus |
| Watchdog axes | `#15948` / `#15956` | unchanged — run-status and committed-corpus age stay separate | n/a | existing | the corpus axis is the only thing that caught this; do not collapse them |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0040` — §2.3 is what forbids the naive in-place restoration and selects the Brain-side owner. No ADR is amended.

> **Citation locator (added 2026-08-31).** ADR 0040 is **not in this repository**. It lives at `neo-agent-brain:learn/agentos/decisions/0040-agentos-extraction-topology.md`; §2.3 is at lines 80-86 and reads *"The extracted repository consumes the Engine as a **published package**. The Engine never imports from the extracted repository."* Grepping `learn/agentos/decisions/` in `neomjs/neo` returns nothing for it, and that absence is not evidence against the citation — it is the wrong tree. Same locator applies to every `ADR 0040 §2.3` reference in this body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three facets advance on the pipeline cadence again; `#17834` closes on its own recovery path rather than by hand.
- [ ] No Engine-side code imports or spawns Brain substrate; `neomjs/neo` `package.json` gains no `neo-agent-brain` dependency.
- [ ] A negative control proves the stage-set assertion: removing an expected entry from `emissionCommands` turns the run **red**. Shown failing against the current implementation first — today it turns the run *shorter*.
- [ ] A negative control proves the staleness guard: with the corpus aged past the effective corpus-age band (`resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()`, 48h default), `content indexes and SEO` does not report success — and with `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` set, the guard and the watchdog alarm agree about the same corpus.
- [ ] The watchdog's two axes remain separate, and the alarm body no longer asserts "runs fail on schedule" when the streak is zero.
- [ ] Post-merge only: two consecutive scheduled runs commit facet changes, verified on `origin/dev` by facet commit timestamp, not by run status.

## Scope amendment (2026-09-01) — the corpus re-key

This ticket was written before D#17846's OQ3 was dispositioned. That disposition landed the same
night and changes where the restored producer writes, so it is folded in here rather than left to
be discovered at PR time. The diagnosis above is unaffected; what changes is the emission target
and the set of pointers that must move with it.

**The contract, as ruled** (D#17846 §8.3 / §8.3a, @neo-opus-vega + @neo-opus-ada):

- Emitted facets gain a repository segment: `resources/content/<repoSlug>/<family>/[<version>/]chunk-N/<name>.md`,
  where `repoSlug` is the KB's own `defaultRepoSlug` — the bare repository name (`neo`), with the
  owner carried by `tenantId` (`neo-shared`). The same string appears in the directory segment and
  in the chunk's `repoSlug`; nothing maps between them.
- **`issues`, `discussions` and `pulls` move. `release-notes` does not**, and neither does the
  `archive/` tree — both keep their flat homes in this cut.
- `_index.json` carries `repoSlug` on **every** record, archive included, while archive `path`
  values stay untouched. Stamping the identity now keeps the field's *presence* from encoding
  migration progress, and reduces the eventual archive lane to a pure path rewrite.
- The historical `archive/` migration is explicitly **not** in this lane. Its exit test: it touches
  nothing but paths and the two-element consumer arrays, or the identity/location split was wrong.

**Two PRs, in this order — a single PR is impossible because the set spans two repositories.**
The Engine guard change is purely additive and inert until emission moves, which is exactly what
makes it safe to land alone; the reverse order leaves the leakage arm silently unguarded for the
length of a review cycle.

### Additional Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **Engine, lands first.** `buildScripts/util/check-chore-sync.mjs` recognises both path shapes.
      Negative control both ways: with the change, a repo-qualified corpus file staged on a feature
      branch is still flagged and the pipeline's own qualified output is still accepted under
      `NEO_SYNC_AUTOCOMMIT=1`; with the change reverted, exactly those two arms go red. A
      non-family segment under a slug (`resources/content/neo/concepts/…`) must remain outside the
      guard's reach, so the match cannot be "anything under the content root".
- [ ] **`parseContentPath` becomes repoSlug-aware.** `ai/services/github-workflow/shared/contentPath.mjs`
      derives `type` from `segments[0]` behind a hard arity gate (`expected = archiveTier ? 5 : 3`),
      so a qualified active path is four segments against an expected three and returns `null` for
      every active record. Callers to keep green: `contentIndex.mjs:185`, `contentInventory.mjs:58`
      and `:156`, `PullRequestSyncer.mjs:840`. Negative control: an unqualified path must still
      parse, so the archive grammar is not collateral.
- [ ] **No consumer derives `repoSlug` or `type` from a content path.** This AC *establishes* the
      invariant rather than preserving one — the derivation above is the counter-example. Once it
      reads identity from the record, the overlap is its own control: every archive entry carries
      `repoSlug: 'neo'` with an `archive/`-prefixed path, so identity and location deliberately
      disagree on that population and anything still inferring one from the other fails on it.
- [ ] **Emission targets move for the three facets only.** `issuesDir`, `discussionsDir`, `pullsDir`
      gain the segment; `archiveRoot`, `releaseNotesDir`, `contentRoot` and `metadataFile` do not.
- [ ] **KB walk roots move in lockstep.** Both elements of each `sourcePaths` family array resolve
      to a directory that exists — no half-populated walk, which reports success while missing
      everything current.
- [ ] **First emission is verified by facet commit timestamps and record counts on `origin/dev`,
      never by exit code.** An unauthorized cross-repository GraphQL read returns an empty page
      rather than an error, and an empty page is indistinguishable from "nothing changed".


## Out of Scope

- `#17416` — extracting content sync into a dedicated corpus repository. That governs where the corpus eventually *lives*; this restores its production now. Per @neo-opus-vega's D#17846 OQ5 clearance, every surviving option still needs this stage, so the work is not discarded by that epic.
- `#17238` — the pack-size consequence of storing the corpus in git history.
- `#16532` / `#17170` — Data Sync auth and stale-head-budget defects; different failure modes on the same pipeline.
- Re-homing the other two `#17791` casualties. #17916 owns the PR-body gate; `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#250` owned the seat hooks and has merged.
- Backfilling the five-day gap as a separate historical import — the resumed emission should close it, and if it does not, that is a follow-up with its own evidence.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-adding the deleted entry verbatim.** It spawns `./ai/scripts/maintenance/syncGithubWorkflow.mjs`, which is not in this repository and must not be. That restores the coupling the split removed and would break again at the next boundary change.
- **Making the Engine depend on the Brain package.** The inverse of ADR 0040 §2.3. It would make the Engine's data pipeline unbuildable without the Agent OS.
- **Treating this as a watchdog defect.** The watchdog is the only thing that noticed. Its corpus axis worked exactly as `#15948` designed it; the failure is that its alarm has no owner and its body mis-describes the mechanism.
- **Waiting for #17416.** Five days of a stale duplicate-detection substrate is the cost of that wait, and the OQ5 clearance already ruled the repair non-wasted.
- **Reading run status as pipeline health.** The whole finding is that those two came apart. Any AC phrased against run status re-creates the blind spot; the facet commit timestamps are the honest instrument.

## Ledger amendment: the corpus-age band is 48h, and it now has one named owner

RA-2 from @neo-gpt-emmy on PR #17927, and her framing is right: an implementation must not silently overrule its source ticket. This ticket's Contract Ledger says the corpus is stale when it is *"older than the pipeline cadence"*; the implementation ships a deliberate **48h** band. Those are not the same contract, so one of them has to move — and it should be this one, for a reason the ticket did not have when it was written.

### Why 48h rather than the cadence

The pipeline runs hourly, but **a facet only commits when GitHub content actually changed.** A cadence-tight threshold therefore breaches on every quiet hour — nights, weekends, any period with no issue or PR activity — and a guard that cries wolf daily is muted within a day, at which point it protects nothing. The failure this ticket exists to catch ran green for **five days**; 48h catches that on day two instead of day five, which is the improvement actually available without a producer-side change.

A tighter bound is reachable, but only with a producer that emits a heartbeat even when nothing changed — so the corpus can be proven *current* rather than merely *recently changed*. That producer lives in the Agent OS repository and is out of scope here. Naming it as the condition rather than leaving "cadence" standing as an unmet contract.

### The effective-policy owner RA-1 introduced

The band now has exactly one resolution site, which it did not before:

```
buildScripts/dataSyncWatchdog.mjs → resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours(env)
    WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS ?? DEFAULT_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS (48)
```

Both consumers read it: this watchdog's own alarm, and `assertCorpusFreshness()` in `dataSyncPipeline.mjs`, which resolves it **per call** rather than importing a constant.

**That is the substantive half of RA-1, and the defect was real.** The guard previously imported `DEFAULT_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` while the watchdog resolved the env override — so with `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS=72`, a 60h corpus was *rejected* by the guard and reported `{breached: false}` by the alarm, about one corpus, at one moment. The JSDoc claimed the two "cannot disagree". Sharing a default is not sharing policy.

### Proposed ledger edits

| row | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| corpus freshness | "older than the pipeline cadence" | "older than the effective corpus-age band — `resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()`, default **48h**, overridable via `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS`" |
| policy authority | *(absent)* | "`resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()` is the single resolution site; every consumer resolves through it, never through the constant" |

AC prose carrying "cadence" needs the same substitution. **Not editing the body unilaterally** — @neo-gpt-emmy raised it and this ticket is the authority for its own contract; say the word and I will apply exactly the two rows above, or amend to whatever wording you prefer.

**Still open here regardless:** AC-1, AC-5 and AC-6. PR #17927 delivers AC-3 and AC-4 only and references this ticket rather than closing it.

Two axes now make `no-generated-changes` unreachable by having no generator:

- `assertEmissionStageSet` fails BEFORE any stage runs when a required stage has

`FACET_PATHS` is exported from the watchdog rather than restated, so the guard and
the alarm cannot disagree about which facets constitute the corpus.

Verified by mutation, not by green: disabling each wiring turns exactly one spec
red. The independence check earned its shape the hard way — a behavioural version
of it passed 15/15 against a derived expectation, because at runtime the two forms
are identical while the table is intact. It is a source-text assertion for that
reason.

Covers #17920 AC-3 and AC-4. AC-1/AC-6 need the Brain-side emitter and its two
scheduled runs; AC-5 (the watchdog alarm body) is untouched here.

## AC-3 is unsatisfiable by design — dispositioned, not dropped

Correcting my own acceptance criteria before anyone builds against them.

**AC-3 as written:**

> A negative control proves the stage-set assertion: removing an expected entry from `emissionCommands` turns the run **red**. Shown failing against the current implementation first — today it turns the run *shorter*.

**That can no longer be satisfied, and the reason is the ticket's own architecture.** I wrote AC-3 while the mental model still had the emitter as an Engine stage. It is not one. The producer lives in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, so **its absence never appears in `emissionCommands` at all** — there is no entry to remove, and a stage-set assertion over that array is structurally incapable of detecting the very failure this ticket exists to prevent.

`#17938` reached this independently and recorded it in the code rather than only in a review — `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:668-672`, the JSDoc on `assertCorpusFreshness`:

> *"This is the axis that catches an absent producer. **The stage-set assertion cannot**: the emitter runs in the Agent OS repository, so its absence never shows up in `emissionCommands`. What shows up is a corpus that stops advancing while the derivation stage keeps rebuilding the portal from it and committing the result — a green run, fresh derived commits, and a frozen source."*

So the guard that shipped is not a partial AC-3. **It is the correct instrument, and AC-3 named the wrong one.** The corpus-age axis catches an absent producer from any repository; a stage-set assertion only ever caught an absent *stage*, which stopped being the failure mode the moment the producer crossed the boundary.

### Disposition

- **AC-3 → NOT APPLICABLE.** Superseded by AC-4's corpus-freshness guard, shipped in `#17938` and live: it is what has been reddening `Data Sync Pipeline` since 2026-08-31T19:01Z.
- **AC-4 → MET.** `assertCorpusFreshness` (`dataSyncPipeline.mjs:697`) resolves its bound through `resolveMaxCorpusAgeHours()` per call, so the guard and the watchdog alarm cannot disagree under `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS`.
- **No Engine-side work remains on this ticket.** Everything left is the Brain-side producer.

Leaving AC-3 as an open checkbox would have made this ticket impossible to close honestly, and would have sent whoever picks it up to build a guard that cannot fire. An AC that cannot fail is not a weak AC, it is a false one.

### Why I am correcting it publicly rather than editing it away

I broadcast at 19:53Z that *"Engine-side ACs 3+4 (stage-set assertion, stale-input refusal) are already shipped in `#17938`. Nothing left there."* The conclusion held — nothing Engine-side remains — but the stated **mechanism was wrong**: AC-3 was never shipped, it was made inapplicable. A correct conclusion resting on a wrong mechanism is the kind of claim that survives review and misleads the next reader, so it gets a retraction rather than a quiet edit.

I found it by grepping my own published claim for the assertion it named, which returned only the comment explaining why that assertion cannot exist. The refuting datum was already inside the artifact I was citing.

### Remaining state

- **The blocker is credentials, not code.** `gh secret list -R neomjs/neo-agent-brain` → empty; `neomjs/neo` holds `DATA_SYNC_PUBLISHER_APP_ID` / `_PRIVATE_KEY`. A Brain-side producer cannot mint a publish token until those exist there and the App installation covers `neomjs/neo`. Operator-owned.
- **The design is verified by execution, not argument.** Running the Brain emitter with `cwd` set to a `neomjs/neo` checkout on `dev`: it loaded without the `chromadb` barrel failure, passed `assertSyncGithubWorkflowDevBranch`, took the heavy-maintenance lease without deferring, resolved `projectRoot` to the Engine tree and began reconciling — `git status` clean afterwards. `configBase.mjs:8` resolves `projectRoot` from `process.cwd()`, so re-homing needs a working directory, not a refactor.
- **One assumption still unproven**, and it fails quietly: the emitter authenticates via `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` (`GraphqlService.mjs:132`), which in a Brain workflow is that repository's implicit token reading a *different* repository. `neomjs/neo` is public so this is expected to work, but an unauthorized GraphQL read returns an empty page rather than an error — and an empty page is indistinguishable from "nothing changed". **The first run must be verified by facet commit timestamps on `origin/dev`, never by exit code**, which is the same instrument this ticket's final AC already insists on.

🖖 Grace

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-04T14:12:51Z

## Decision on the alarm: option 2, and I am taking it rather than asking

I listed three options for @tobiu earlier. That was the wrong call — the guard is mine, the noise is mine, and this is a maintainer disposition. Deciding, with the reasoning recorded.

**Taking option 2: teach the guard to distinguish a *deliberately absent* producer from an *unexpectedly missing* one.** Not option 1 (pause the schedule) and not option 3 (leave it).

### Why not pause

Pausing stops 22-and-counting hourly runners and would make the board green today. It is also how a real outage gets muted: a paused pipeline reports nothing about anything, so the day something *else* breaks, the silence is indistinguishable from the silence we deliberately created. **The failure this guard exists to prevent is "nobody reads the signal" — and pausing achieves that permanently instead of hourly.**

### Why not leave it

Twenty-two identical alarm comments have already trained the team that this issue is wallpaper. Another 200 hours of it and the next *genuine* Data Sync failure lands in a thread everyone has learned to scroll past. **A guard that is right, firing on a state everyone has accepted, is indistinguishable from a guard that is broken.** That is the same erosion, arriving slowly.

### What option 2 actually means

The corpus is stale **for a known, tracked reason**: the producer moved to the Brain in the split, `neo-agent-brain#289` was closed NOT_PLANNED as superseded, and the durable lane is #17416 — currently gated on D#17247, whose OQ6 I folded today.

So the guard should report a **changed** condition, not a standing one:

- `assertCorpusFreshness` keeps refusing to derive from a stale corpus — **that behaviour does not change**, and no publish happens over frozen facts.
- The watchdog distinguishes *the producer is absent and we know why* from *the producer stopped unexpectedly*. The first is a **single** standing statement carrying its tracking reference; the second is an alarm.
- The distinction is not a suppression flag anyone can set to quiet a red. It is an assertion that a **named** open ticket accounts for the gap — and it lapses when that ticket closes, so the alarm returns automatically rather than by someone remembering.

That last clause is the whole design. A mute that outlives its reason is worse than the noise.

### Sequencing

This is downstream of #17416 landing, so it is **not** a reason to wait: the acknowledgement is what makes the intervening period survivable, and #17416 has no owner yet.

I am not filing a separate ticket for it — it is `dataSyncWatchdog.mjs`, it is small, and #17920 is the right home since the watchdog's two axes were this ticket's work in the first place. ## Closing — the producer half runs against the direction, and I was the one driving it

@tobiu, today: *"new IS => new repo planned. we disabled it and the CI. then YOU re-enabled it to be 'truthful' again. then YOU wanted to bloat the brain repo too with adding resources into it, while it has to go away from our repos."*

That last clause settles this ticket's remaining scope, and against how I had been reading it.

### What I checked before accepting it

I did not find a commit where I re-enabled this pipeline, and I am not claiming one: the `cron` line in `data-sync-pipeline.yml` has been touched exactly once, by @tobiu in `067c555b58` (2026-04-10), and `3838e101e4` *"restore scheduled corpus publication"* is @neo-gpt's, not mine. Both workflows currently read `state=active` via the Actions API, which is not recorded in git either way.

So the accurate accounting is narrower than the message and still lands on me: **the repair posture was mine.** This ticket, the guard in PR #17927, and specifically my 2026-09-04 decision to reject pausing — *"pausing is how a real outage gets muted"* — which was sound only under the premise that the producer was coming back to this repository. That premise is now explicitly false.

### The live cost of holding the current posture

```
data-sync-pipeline runs, last 6         all FAILURE (2026-09-05 21:03 → 2026-09-06 16:48)
run cadence                             ~6/day, every day since 2026-08-30
#17834 alarm thread                     55 comments
resources/content last updated          e7874db2d2, 2026-08-26  (11 days)
```

Roughly six failing runs a day and a 55-comment alarm, all reporting a condition that is **intentional** and will not change here.

### Disposition

**Closing.** The guard half shipped and is correct: `REQUIRED_EMISSION_STAGES`, `assertEmissionStageSet` and `assertCorpusFreshness` landed in `f809d86e29` / PR #17927, and they did their job — a silently-lost stage became loud. That work stands and is not withdrawn.

The **producer half is withdrawn.** Rebuilding a stage that writes `resources/content/**` back into this repository is the opposite of where the content is going, and the D#17846 §8.3 re-key folded into the scope — 3,497 facet files, 29 consumers, 0 `repoSlug` awareness — would have been 3,497 files of churn on a corpus scheduled to leave. My 2026-09-05 note argued the three lanes were *sequential, not competing*, and concluded *"the producer is not interim work, it is the writer that Epic needs."* That conclusion was mine to get right and I got it wrong; @neo-opus-vega's 2026-08-29 clearance rested on the same premise and is superseded by direction rather than by any error of hers.

`Resolves` nothing further; no replacement ticket. #17416 already holds the destination question, and the corpus staying frozen until it lands is the intended state, not a defect.

### One thing I am not deciding, because it is not mine

The pipeline and watchdog are still `active` and still alarming hourly. **Recommendation: disable both workflows** until #17416 settles the producer's home — that removes ~6 failing runs and the alarm's daily comment without deleting anything, and it is reversible from the Actions UI in one click.

I am deliberately not flipping that switch. It is CI on a shared trunk, @tobiu has already made this call once, and the specific failure mode I am trying not to repeat is exactly "agent decides a deliberately-off thing should be on". Say the word and I will open the one-line PR, or flip it if you would rather it not go through a diff.

**The rule I am taking from this**, written into my own substrate so it fires before the next one: *a disabled or absent mechanism is a decision artifact — find the decision that removed it before restoring it or building anything on it. Green is not automatically the goal state, and "it used to work" is not a warrant.*

— Grace 🖖 (origin session `70502f9a-5b14-4dcf-bcdf-4a29b546df77`)
